# CourtLine Android 1.0.23: administrator-directed device recovery

Requires Backend 0.36.0-test.54 or later for recovery. Existing pairing and reconnection remain compatible.

The Backend administrator can select an existing active device record and issue a five-minute, single-use recovery QR. Android explicitly confirms that record and replacement of prior app access. It verifies the physical QR certificate pin and Backend identity before sending the recovery ticket over HTTPS. A verified response must identify the selected family, Companion role, and a valid replacement viewer credential before the app saves its new connection and trust.

Recovery keeps the Backend record name, Control permission and individual PIN policy; it does not immediately enter Control. The previous installation's viewer and Control credentials stop working. Lost responses require a fresh owner-issued recovery QR for the same record, never a new-device enrollment fallback. Names/models are not identity evidence. Ordinary enrollment, safe Secure Reconnect and discovery retain their existing rules.

Validation: 55 existing non-browser tests pass; added real Backend prototype integration decodes the owner-issued QR, uses the shipped Java TLS verifier and exercises same-family recovery, no duplicate rows, retained Control permission and PIN promotion, old viewer/main revocation, unrelated device isolation, single use, HTTPS-only redemption, remote owner-route denial, wrong-pin rejection, and owner reissue after response loss. Physical Android UI/camera and production Backend bundle acceptance remain pending.

The recovery-response-loss test verifies owner reissue following successful server consumption, not a physical dropped-response Android lifecycle. Owner cancellation is tied to the specific issuance, so an older dialog cannot invalidate a newer recovery ticket.
